subject: ss-cardiology
title: Device Therapy, Mechanical Support and Transplantation

steps.tx: **Cardiac resynchronization therapy** is indicated for symptomatic heart failure despite medical therapy with LVEF at most **35%**, sinus rhythm, and **left bundle branch block** with QRS duration at least **150** ms as a Class I recommendation. Biventricular pacing coordinates ventricular contraction, reversing progressive adverse chamber remodeling and reducing hospitalizations.

steps.tx: The radiograph shows a left sided **pulse generator** connected to three transvenous leads that pace both ventricles and provide backup **defibrillation**. The thin **right atrial** lead rests in the atrial appendage, the thick coil bearing lead sits at the **right ventricular** apex, and the third lead courses through the coronary sinus to the lateral left ventricular wall. This arrangement restores coordinated contraction in suitable symptomatic patients despite medical therapy.
steps.say: This chest radiograph shows a pulse generator below the left collarbone with three leads. One thin lead ends in the right atrium, one thick lead with a shock coil ends at the right ventricular apex, and one lead passes through the coronary sinus to pace the lateral wall of the left ventricle. Together they deliver coordinated biventricular pacing with defibrillator backup for selected patients who remain symptomatic despite medical therapy.

steps.tx: An **Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator** is indicated for **primary prevention** in ischemic cardiomyopathy with LVEF at most **35%** at least **40** days post-MI and after 90 days of revascularisation, or non-ischemic cardiomyopathy after **3** months of optimal therapy. Prophylactic ICD deployment protects against fatal ventricular tachyarrhythmias.
steps.say: An Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator is indicated for primary prevention in ischemic cardiomyopathy with LVEF under 35% at least 40 days post-MI and after 90 days of revascularisation, or non-ischemic cardiomyopathy after 3 months of optimal therapy. Prophylactic ICD deployment protects vulnerable patients against fatal ventricular tachyarrhythmias and helps prevent sudden cardiac death.

steps.tx: The **Subcutaneous ICD** eliminates intravascular and **transvenous lead** complications, proving ideal for patients lacking bradycardia pacing requirements or antitachycardia pacing needs. Transvenous lead extraction complications and endovascular lead endocarditis are completely avoided with an entirely extravascular pulse generator and subcutaneous parasternal electrode.

left.title: Subcutaneous ICD (S-ICD)
points: Entirely subcutaneous pulse generator and lead
Zero risk of vascular occlusion or systemic lead sepsis
Cannot provide bradycardia pacing (except post-shock)
Cannot deliver antitachycardia pacing (ATP) for VT

right.title: Transvenous ICD
points: Endovascular lead traversed through subclavian vein into RV
Provides anti-bradycardia and anti-tachycardia pacing
Risk of pneumothorax, cardiac perforation, lead fracture
Lead extraction carries significant morbidity

steps.tx: The **Intra-aortic balloon pump** provides diastolic **counterpulsation** by inflating during early diastole at the dicrotic notch to augment coronary blood flow, and deflating immediately before systole to reduce left ventricular afterload. Counterpulsation unloads the failing left ventricle, though routine deployment in post-MI shock lacks mortality reduction.
steps.say: The Intra-aortic balloon pump provides diastolic counterpulsation by inflating during early diastole at the dicrotic notch to augment coronary blood flow, and deflating immediately before systole to reduce left ventricular afterload. Counterpulsation unloads the failing left ventricle, though routine deployment in post-MI shock lacks mortality reduction.

left.title: Diastolic Balloon Inflation
points: Inflates immediately at dicrotic notch
Augments central aortic diastolic pressure
Enhances coronary and cerebral arterial perfusion
Increases systemic oxygen delivery

right.title: Presystolic Balloon Deflation
points: Deflates immediately before aortic valve opening
Creates vacuum effect reducing LV afterload
Decreases left ventricular end-systolic wall stress
Lowers myocardial oxygen consumption

steps.tx: The left panel shows the balloon inflated in the descending aorta during diastole, boosting **coronary flow** as the pressure tracing shows assisted diastolic augmentation. The right panel shows it deflated just before systole, producing an **afterload fall** that unloads the ventricle. This timed **counterpulsation** explains the lesson point that inflation aids perfusion while deflation eases ejection.
steps.say: Watch the two phases in order. First the balloon fills right after the aortic valve closes, pushing blood back toward the coronary arteries when they fill. Then it collapses just before the heart squeezes, leaving a low pressure space that makes ejection easier. One phase feeds the heart muscle, the other lightens its workload, which is the whole logic of counterpulsation.

vis.alt: Two panel illustration shows an aortic balloon inflated in diastole boosting coronary flow and deflated before systole lowering afterload.
vis.caption: Paired panels showing diastolic balloon inflation then presystolic deflation for counterpulsation, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Impella** is a percutaneous transvalvular **microaxial** flow pump delivering up to **2.5** to **5.5** L/min of forward blood flow directly from left ventricle to ascending aorta, unloading the ventricle and reducing myocardial oxygen consumption. It directly draws blood across the aortic valve, decreasing end-diastolic wall tension.
steps.say: Impella is a percutaneous transvalvular microaxial flow pump delivering up to 2 point 5 to 5 point 5 L/min of forward blood flow directly from left ventricle to ascending aorta, unloading the ventricle and reducing myocardial oxygen consumption. It directly draws blood across the aortic valve, decreasing end-diastolic wall tension.

steps.tx: Venoarterial **extracorporeal membrane oxygenation** provides biventricular support but elevates left ventricular afterload, prompting deployment of combined **ECPELLA** using Impella for active left ventricular venting to prevent hydrostatic pulmonary edema. Unvented retrograde aortic perfusion elevates intracavitary pressures, precipitating stasis and thrombosis. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.

steps.tx: Durable continuous-flow **left ventricular assist devices** like **HeartMate 3** utilize full magnetically levitated centrifugal continuous-flow technology with an artificial pulse, virtually eliminating pump thrombosis and reducing stroke compared to mechanical bearing devices. Frictionless rotor levitation minimizes shear stress, significantly decreasing device malfunction across long-term support.

left.title: HeartMate 3 MagLev Pump
points: Frictionless magnetic rotor levitation
Artificial pulse feature (9000 to 6000 rpm q2s)
Zero pump thrombosis in MOMENTUM 3 trial
Significantly reduced reoperation and stroke

right.title: HeartMate II Mechanical Bearing
points: Axial flow design with mechanical contact cup bearings
Higher shear stress and heat generation
10% to 12% incidence of pump thrombosis
Higher hemolysis and acquired vWF deficiency

steps.tx: Orthotopic **cardiac transplantation** is the gold-standard definitive therapy for refractory end-stage heart failure, yielding a median post-transplant survival of approximately **12** to **14** years with maintenance **calcineurin-inhibitor** immunosuppression. Calcineurin inhibition with tacrolimus or cyclosporine paired with mycophenolate mofetil suppresses T-cell mediated graft rejection.
